newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money slips back to 3.05/3.10 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money slips back to 3.05/3.10 pct.

text.p: German call money eased back to between 3.05 and 3.10 percent on Tuesday after rates tightened sharply on Monday amid a sudden liquidity squeeze.
Traders said liquidity conditions had improved on Tuesday after around 14.5 billion marks was borrowed on the Lombard emergency facility, helping rates stabilise.
Higher daily and monthly reserves also softened rates.
The sharp move up at the beginning of the week could be put down to a bad estimate by the Bundesbank of funds needed in the market, one dealer at a Frankfurt-based bank said.

Daily reserves held by commercial banks at the Bundesbank rose to 57.3 billion marks on Monday, well above Friday's 43.7 billion level. The monthly average was also slightly higher, up at 41.4 billion marks versus 40.9 billion marks on Friday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA rate was quoted at 3.09467 percent on Tuesday after it jumped to 4.50000 percent on Monday.
